idiom_name: module-scoped class with #private fields and readonly properties
implementation_notes: TypeScript inherits the module boundary from ES modules (only exported declarations exist for importers) and adds two member mechanisms: the `private` modifier, which is compile-time only and still reachable through bracket access, and `#` fields, which are hard private at runtime and invisible to reflection and JSON. A standalone class is therefore a module-scoped class whose helpers are not exported, whose state is `readonly` or `#private`, and whose constructor validates; `readonly` arrays and methods returning the class's own type keep callers out of the internals. Types are structural, so a compatible object literal can still be passed where the class is expected - keep the constructor as the only factory, or brand the type, when the invariant must hold.
pitfalls: `private` is soft: bracket notation still reaches the field at runtime, and structural typing accepts a look-alike object literal, so use `#` when the invariant must actually hold.
`readonly` is erased: it stops assignments in type-checked code but a cast or a `JSON.parse` result can still mutate the property, so deep immutability needs explicit copies or `Object.freeze`.
Downlevel targets emulate `#` with `WeakMap`, which changes performance and hides private state from tools expecting plain properties - check the compilation target before relying on hard privacy.
A non-exported module type used in an exported signature breaks declaration emit (the compiler cannot name a private type), so the boundary must be drawn so exported signatures use exported types.
